sections.h2: Where to record a deed in Boyd County
sections.html:
Deeds are recorded with the Boyd County Clerk. The main office is at 2800 Louisa Street in Catlettsburg, and two branches in the Ashland area save sellers on that side of the county a long drive to the seat.

  • Main office, 2800 Louisa Street, Catlettsburg, 606-739-5116, weekdays 8:30 a.m. to 4 p.m.
  • Ashland office, 1505 Carter Avenue, Suite 100, 606-325-3547, weekdays 9:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
  • Cannonsburg office, 1315 Cannonsburg Road, 606-929-9595, weekdays 9 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

Holidays can change those hours. The clerk files land records, wills, liens and lien releases, and articles of incorporation. Phone the branch you plan to visit before you go, especially if the deed still needs a notary, and ask whether that branch takes your kind of document.

Boyd County sits on the Ohio River in the northeastern corner of Kentucky. Ashland is the biggest city and Catlettsburg is the seat. About 47,751 people live here in roughly 21,818 housing units, and owners occupy 70.2% of homes. The typical owner-occupied home is valued at $130,700, and typical rent is $849 a month. Only 12 building permits were issued in 2025, so most competition for a seller comes from other resale houses.

Buyers often ask which school district serves a street. Boyd County Public Schools, Ashland Independent and Fairview Independent each cover part of the county, so know the answer for your address.

sections.h2: What the Boyd County Clerk charges to record
sections.html:
The clerk's fee schedule, dated January 1, 2020, puts a deed at $50 and a mortgage at $80. Extra pages and extra parcel references add to the total, so call 606-739-5116 for today's figure before you mail anything.

Selected recording fees, Boyd County Clerk
Document typeRecording fee
Deed or condo deed$50.00
Deed of correction$46.00
Mortgage$80.00
Release of mortgage$46.00
Affidavit of descent or distribution$50.00
Will$47.00
Judgment lien$46.00
Plat$50.00

Most documents pick up a $3.00 charge for each page after page five. Some items add $4.00 for each extra reference, and a mortgage owes the page charge only after page thirty.

sections.h2: Transfer tax on a Boyd County sale
sections.html:
The foot of the clerk's schedule prints the transfer tax as one dollar for every thousand dollars of value. The seller pays it, and the clerk collects it when the deed is handed in. On the low prices common here, it is usually a smaller line on the settlement statement than the title charges.

Foreclosure transfers, transfers between spouses and token-price family deeds may be exempt. If yours might qualify, ask the clerk before you sign. A deed cannot be accepted until the right amount is paid.

KRS 382.135 lists what a Kentucky deed has to carry: the full names and mailing addresses of both parties, the entire price, and an address for the current year's tax bill.

  • On a sale, both sides sign a notarized oath that the price written in the deed is the price paid.
  • On a gift, the oath says so and gives an estimated fair cash value.
  • The deed refers back to the earlier recorded deed or other source of the seller's title.
  • A deed missing any of these is turned away at the counter.

The seller's source of title is the item that most often goes missing from do-it-yourself deeds. If your house came from a relative years ago and the deed was never recorded, tell your closing attorney at the start. A gap in the chain can hold up a cash closing.

The executor or administrator signs an affidavit naming each person who receives property and what it is worth, then files it with the clerk. On this schedule the affidavit costs $50 and a recorded will costs $47.

Estates can sit for months with a house empty and utilities running. Even a cash buyer needs the record to show who owned the property and who received it. File the affidavit first, then ask the clerk or an attorney what else the county requires.

sections.h2: Closing day at the clerk's counter
sections.html:
Usually a closing attorney or title agent carries in the signed deed, the notarized price certificate and a check for recording and transfer tax. Clerk staff compare the deed with the state's content rules, take the tax, stamp the date and amount on the deed and file it.

Expect a few small costs beyond the deed fee. If a mortgage is being paid off, its release lists at $46 and is recorded after closing. Add transfer tax and any page charges, and your closing agent can give you the real total.

  1. Gather the deed, the notarized oath and the payoff letter if there is a mortgage.
  2. Confirm the fee and the branch with the clerk.
  3. Pay recording and transfer tax when the deed is filed.
  4. Keep the stamped copy once it is returned.

sections.h2: Before you go to the clerk
sections.html:
A little preparation saves a second trip. Most delays at the counter come from a deed that fails the content rules or a check that does not cover everything.

  • Decide which office is closest. The Catlettsburg office is the seat, but Ashland sellers can use Carter Avenue.
  • Check that both parties' names and mailing addresses appear on the deed, along with the tax-bill address.
  • Have the notarized oath signed before you arrive, so you are not hunting for a notary at the last minute.
  • Bring a check large enough for recording, page charges and transfer tax.
  • If a lien or mortgage is being cleared, ask your lender or attorney for the release so it can be recorded too.

Sellers who skip a title company and handle the paperwork themselves should call 606-739-5116 and read the clerk the document list. Staff can tell you what is missing before you pay a notary or drive over.

The County Clerk's office takes over delinquent taxes from earlier years. Call 606-739-5116 and choose option 4.

The Sheriff's Office collects the current year's bill, so an old unpaid bill is a clerk question and this year's bill is a sheriff question. A closing agent checks both before a sale funds. If you know of a delinquent bill, ask the clerk for the payoff amount ahead of time.

sections.h2: Do older Boyd County deeds sit in other counties' books?
sections.html:
Possibly. Boyd County was formed in 1860 from parts of Greenup, Carter and Lawrence Counties, so a chain of title reaching back before that date can lead into the older counties' records. Title examiners follow the chain wherever it goes.

If your family has held the land since the nineteenth century, tell the closing attorney early. A call to the Boyd clerk's main office will show how far back the county's own indexes run.

faqs.q: How do I contact the Boyd County Clerk?
faqs.a: Call 606-739-5116 for the main office at 2800 Louisa Street in Catlettsburg. The Ashland office is 606-325-3547 and the Cannonsburg office is 606-929-9595.

faqs.q: How much does a deed cost to record in Boyd County?
faqs.a: Fifty dollars on the schedule dated January 1, 2020, with $3 added for each page after the fifth. Call to confirm the amount before you mail anything.

faqs.q: What is the transfer tax in Boyd County?
faqs.a: One dollar per thousand dollars of value, printed at the foot of the clerk's schedule. The seller pays it.

faqs.q: Can I record in the Ashland office instead of Catlettsburg?
faqs.a: Possibly. Ashland and Cannonsburg both have County Clerk offices. Call the branch first to confirm it will take your deed.

faqs.q: Where do I pay delinquent Boyd County property taxes from a prior year?
faqs.a: Through the clerk's phone line at 606-739-5116, option 4. This year's bill goes to the sheriff instead.
